backlogged.summary: `node --test` over the full suite showed one transient git 'add failed' error in f9-secret-rename.test.mjs during my first run. The file passes 13/13 when run alone, so it looks like a load or environment flake, not F19.

`endRound` decides whether a failing round is the run's first with `e.history.length > carried`, which relies on `history` and `carried` staying in sync. A short comment or a dedicated `firstRunRound` flag would make that clearer.

When run blocks with `max_rounds` before any round (SC-1), it sets `e.round = e.carried` and reports 'N of M rounds ... already evaluated'. That is correct, but the state is set inside `runOne` as a side effect. Consider moving the check next to the carry-over setup.
`verify.test_count` is unset, so the harness does not check whether the test count decreases. Consider setting it.

The SC-1 early block in runOne only fires when e.stage === 'worktree'. A resumed run keeps its saved e.carried/e.round, so this is consistent today. But if a future change resets the stage on resume, the carried-rounds guard could be skipped. Consider asserting the round limit wherever e.round is incremented.

Carried eval_error verdicts count toward `carried` (the round limit) but add an empty blocking set to history and set carriedPrev to null. The run's evalErrors counter still starts at 0, so consecutive eval_error verdicts from interactive eval are not carried into MAX_EVAL_ERRORS. The contract does not cover this.

Before starting a feature, the run re-reads every verdict file of that feature, including files from other contract hashes. A corrupt verdict from an old contract therefore stops the run with state_corrupt, even though it is outside the current hash. This matches the existing E6 behavior of contractVerdicts, but it is stricter than ES-1 requires.
